advisory: A pre-1955 lay hand missal's Ordinary, and never a book to celebrate from. The English here is the anonymous translation an 1861 Philadelphia printing made for the laity to follow the Mass with; it is not an approved liturgical translation, it was never an altar book, and nothing in it may be used for recitation. It is carried under the 1962 Missal because the Ordinary is substantially the same rite, but it is a witness to the discipline in force before the 1955 and 1960 reforms, and it differs from the 1962 typical edition in orthography and in some rubrics. Six blocks whose own source rows say in terms that the 1962 Ordo Missae does not contain them, and the six blocks of the second-Postcommunion regime and the added prayer Et famulos that the verified 1962 Ordo passages show it does not print, are excluded from the target frame and retained in its explicit exclusion accounting; a difference that does not establish non-membership remains an uncollated antecedent. Both of the book's columns are now transcribed: the Latin named below is the 1861 printing's own, read from the facing column of the same openings, and it is a pre-1955 witness to the rite and never the text of the 1962 typical edition - its Communicantes prints no clause naming St Joseph, its Prefaces are the eleven this book knew, and its spelling, its j and its ae and oe ligatures are its own. Where the book sets a block across the full measure in English and prints no facing Latin at all, that silence is the witness's own and the element says so. Where the 1962 Missal appoints a text the 1861 book does not print, or prints differently, the element names its own witness: the proper Communicantes and Hanc igitur of Pentecost and Easter and the continuation the 1962 Canon prints for every Communicantes come from a project editorial projection over public-domain printings, and the Hanc igitur's English from the Lasance hand missal.

appointments.what: Which of the sixteen Prefaces of RGMR 484-499 the day takes: RGMR 482, the Preface proper to the Mass, failing it the Preface de Tempore, otherwise the common Preface, and RGMR 483, no commemoration brings in a proper Preface. Step one is the celebrated formulary's own printed direction, recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml as `ordinary_appointments` (a feria borrowing a formulary does not take it). Step two is the Preface de Tempore, stated below as the dated spans of the b) clauses of RGMR 484-493: it reaches every Mass of its window that prints no direction, which is RGMR's 'in ceteris Missis ... quae praefatione propria carent'. RGMR 494 b), the Trinity Preface on Sundays, is carried by the Sunday formularies' own printed directions and not by a span, because its reach is the Mass of the Sunday and not every Mass said on one. Step three is the common Preface (RGMR 482, 498).

slots_derived_from: Where each proper of the day stands inside this frame is read from the 1962 typical edition itself - the Ritus servandus in celebratione Missae and the Ordo Missae - and not from the 1861 witness whose words the elements carry. Each slot names the paragraph of the Ritus servandus that states the place; where the position of a seasonal chant is stated instead by a rubric of the Proprium de Tempore, the slot names that rubric beside it, by its marginal number and printed page. The two books agree on the order of these nine positions, which is why the anchors below are 1861 elements and the loci are 1962 rubrics; where they did not agree, no slot would be declared.
